content.overview: Article 54 provides that the President shall be elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of (a) the elected members of both Houses of Parliament; and (b) the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States. (Nominated members do not form part of the electoral college.)
content.glance: President elected by electoral college: elected MPs (both Houses) + elected MLAs of States.
content.study:
Article 54:
The President shall be elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of—
(a) the elected members of both Houses of Parliament; and
(b) the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.

Manner of election (system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote; voting by secret ballot) is under Article 55.

Nominated members of Parliament and of State Legislative Assemblies are not part of the electoral college. Union territory Legislative Assemblies’ elected members have been brought into the framework by constitutional amendment/practice as applicable.

Examination: elected MPs + elected State MLAs; exclude nominated members; link Art 55 for manner.

sections.heading: Electoral college
sections.body:
1. Elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
2. Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.
3. Nominated members are not included.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Who elects the President under Article 54?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 54, the President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States. Nominated members are not part of the electoral college.

examTips: Elected MPs + elected State MLAs; no nominated members.

keyTakeaways: Art 54: electoral college = elected MPs + elected State MLAs.
